articles.title: How connections have shaped us
articles.summary: The world today is a big interconnected village.
articles.body: The world today is a big interconnected village. Notwithstanding some political impulses to ‘pull up the drawbridge’, the sinews of globalisation run deep, whether through trade, climate or politics. Actually, the arteries of this globalised world have been millennia in the making. In Earth Shapers:How Humans Mastered Geography & Remade The World, author Maxim Samson takes a deeper look at these connections, not just analysing them , but also their physicalimpact on earth, the legacy they leave behind, and how they shape, and were shaped by, societies and international politics.Samson’s story begins in a tiny town in Libya called Ras Lanuf, which saw fierce battles at the height of the Libyan civil war in the last decade. But its roots go back to 4th century BC, when the Carthaginians and Cyreneans drew up their borders at the site of this town. Two millennia later, Mussolini would erect a triumphal arch at the very location.But Ras Lanuf would have another distinction: it would be the central pivot of a massive engineering project conceived by the Italian colonists – the Libyan Coastal Highway that stretched nearly 2,000km from Tunisia in the west to Egypt in the east, along Libya’s Mediterranean coast. Libya under Gaddafi dynamited Mussolini’s arch at Ras Lanuf. But, the highway still remains a major terrestrial artery in the region.Similarly, the mindboggling Inca Highway or Qhapaq Nan in South America, stretching over a mammoth 40,000km across the Andes Mountains, connecting the Amazon Rainforest with the Atacama Desert, was a symbol of power and prestige for the Inca Empire. Per the author, Incas used the highway to not just exert control over their vast territories, but also to integrate newly conquered lands and peoples. But the same Great Highway would be repurposed by the Spanish conquistadors, for rampant extraction of minerals and gold, riches found in abundance in South American lands.The author’s thesis, that grand connective infra can be reoriented to serve very different political interests over centuries, is a theme that runs across the book. This is again vividly seen in Mozambique, where once-colonial power Portugal built a disjointed railway infra that was solely aimed at reasserting Portuguese power, and for extracting resources – the legacy of which burdens Mozambicans even today.In the western hemisphere, the Panama Canal – another feat of grand engineering – may not have happened at all. The French tried to build the canal first, but failed miserably. Then Americans debated an alternative route via Nicaragua.But after TheodoreRoosevelt insisted onPanama, Washington supported an insurrection in the region against Colombia, and imposed onerous conditions on the new Panama state, to both construct and control the canal – impacting climate, and millions of lives in the region.Of course, not all connections are permanently physical or exploitative, per the author. The Baltic Way human chain in 1989 – spanning 700km, and involving around 2mn people – saw the residents of the Baltic nations of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania lock arms in a show of solidarity, and to protest against Soviet Union, exemplifying connections as a form of resistance.In sum, humans will always seek to connect. Plus, when you break one connection – like the divided Korean Peninsula – yearning for other connections – restoring the spiritual vitality of the inter-Korean Baekdu-daegan mountain range – take root.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Alaska Energy Authority disbursed about $46 million in Power Cost Equalization payments during fiscal year 2025 to help reduce electricity costs for rural
articles.body: Alaska Energy Authority disbursed about $46 million in Power Cost Equalization payments during fiscal year 2025 to help reduce electricity costs for rural residents and community facilities across the state. The programme serves more than 81,000 Alaskans in 188 primarily diesel-dependent communities, with customers in 186 communities benefiting from PCE credits.According to the 2025 AEA Annual Report (Alaska Energy Authority), the payments support rural residents while also helping the long-term viability of utilities serving Alaska’s most remote communities. AEA administers the programme by providing payments to eligible rural electric utilities, which apply credits to qualifying residential and community facility customers. The programme was established in 1984 to bring rural electricity costs closer to those paid in Alaska’s larger cities.How did Alaska spend about $46 million to lower electricity costsThe Power Cost Equalization Program was established in 1984 to reduce electricity costs for rural residents and community facilities to levels comparable to those paid in Alaska’s larger cities.AEA administers the programme for more than 81,000 Alaskans in 188 primarily diesel-dependent communities. Residential and community facility customers in 186 communities benefit from PCE credits. AEA calculates payments using monthly utility filings and disburses the money to eligible utilities.The utilities then apply credits to qualifying customers for electricity use up to specified consumption limits. In fiscal year 2025, AEA disbursed about $46 million in PCE payments to rural utilities. The payments help ease electricity costs for residents and community facilities while supporting long-term viability of utilities serving remote communities.Alaska’s endowment fund helps finance rural electricity supportPCE payments are funded by the PCE Endowment Fund. Alaska Statute 42.45.085 authorises the Legislature to appropriate up to five percent of the fund’s three-year average market value for PCE payments.In recent years, the five-percent draw has fully funded PCE disbursements. Statutory changes enacted in fiscal year 2018 established how excess earnings are allocated. These changes allow endowment earnings to fully cover PCE programme administrative costs and direct $30 million annually to the Community Assistance Program.The statute also authorises up to $25 million to support the Renewable Energy Fund, Rural Power System Upgrade projects, and the Alaska Division of Community and Regional Affairs’ Bulk Fuel Revolving Loan Fund.How does Alaska’s Power Cost Equalization programme help rural customersThe programme provides different electricity credit limits for residential customers and public facilities. Residential customers may receive PCE credit for up to 750 kilowatt-hours per month. Community facilities may receive PCE credit of 70 kilowatt-hours per month multiplied by the number of residents.The programme works through eligible rural electric utilities, which receive payments from AEA and apply credits to qualifying customers. In many rural communities, electricity rates before PCE exceed urban rates. AEA’s PCE team also provides technical assistance to utility clerks to support accurate reporting and filing. This administration allows the programme to calculate and distribute payments based on monthly utility filings while maintaining the credit structure for participating customers and community facilities across rural Alaska.How can modern fuel facilities help lower energy costs in rural AlaskaRural Alaska relies heavily on diesel fuel for power generation and heating, and many villages depend on barges to deliver fuel for diesel-fired generators and heating. The annual report says rural energy infrastructure also includes bulk fuel facilities that can be more than 40 years old and may exceed their useful life or not meet current standards.AEA’s Rural Power Systems Upgrade and Bulk Fuel Upgrade programmes address parts of this infrastructure. The report says modern facilities can lower energy costs by preventing leaks and failures, while bulk storage allows communities to purchase fuel in larger quantities.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has stepped up security across the national capital ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed protest against the Election Commission, deploying more than 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel as party activists remain firm on their call for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar.Entry points to the capital have been cordoned off, while 46 metro stations remain closed as authorities seek to prevent a repeat of the July 20 protests.Police personnel deployed for security are wearing body cameras on their uniforms, including devices that can record in the dark. A police personnel told ANI the cameras would help establish what happened during confrontations."These body cams are to protect us and others. In situations of manhandling, allegations are levelled against Delhi Police. So, these body cams will prove whether we did anything to anyone or not. This will record eveything," the personnel said.Dipke questions security crackdown, says ready for arrestCJP founder Abhijeet Dipke left Mumbai for Delhi ahead of the protest and questioned the scale of the security deployment, alleging that it reflected the government's fear of young people and citizens."I feel like the Prime Minister of this country is scared of the youth and the people of this country, and why is he scared? What was the need to shut down all railways, metros, and the internet? You brought the army from Jammu and Kashmir and deployed them in Delhi. You brought CRPF forces from Naxal areas and deployed them in Delhi. Are Narendra Modi and Amit Shah waging a war against their own country's people. Somewhere, this is Narendra Modi's fear," Dipke told ANI.He said the party intended to proceed with its protest peacefully, asserting that the right to protest was protected under Article 19 of the Constitution."Protesting is our fundamental right. Article 19 gives us the fundamental right to protest in a very democratic and peaceful manner, and that is what we are going to do. If they want to detain or arrest me, they can do that. I am ready for it. They can arrest or detain me; it doesn't matter to me. Apply UAPA or NSA, apply it, but we will keep fighting for free and fair elections and to save this country's democracy," he added.Protesters detained as police tighten restrictionsA few protesters were detained near Janpath in the Connaught Place area on Saturday as the CJP called for a large mobilisation at Jantar Mantar despite the Delhi Police denying permission.The proposed demonstration seeks accountability over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. In an Instagram post, the party announced its plan to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“10th October. Jantar Mantar 2.0. We’re coming together again to raise our voice against Gyanesh Kumar. Thousands of us are expected...,” CJP said.Following the announcement, Delhi Police instructed its teams to detain anyone attempting to stage a protest, irrespective of their location. The police have also directed Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) units not to issue weapons for deployment related to the demonstration. Letters have been sent to the concerned directorates regarding the allotment plan.Unlike the deployment during the INDIA bloc protest, police teams have now been authorised to carry lathis and batons. In view of alleged deliberate attempts to record and circulate videos portraying police personnel in a negative light, teams have been instructed to avoid verbal confrontations with protesters.Those detained are to be shifted to six designated centres: Chhatrasal Stadium, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium, Yamuna Sports Complex, Surajmal Stadium, the community centre in Daulatpur and the community centre in Pandrawal.Additional women personnel from Uttar Pradesh and Haryana have also been called in for the October 10 protest.Facial recognition systems, drones among security measuresThe security arrangements also include multiple facial recognition systems (FRS), additional CCTV cameras, rooftop spotters and drones expected to be deployed across central Delhi.The deployment of more than 35,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel comes amid heightened security measures and a directive from the Union home secretary to states and Union Territories to maintain law and order.Authorities are preparing for a large gathering despite the denial of permission, with several student outfits and political groups also expected to join the demonstration.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Trump says he deserves 8 Nobel Peace Prizes, calls award ‘forever discredited’
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday criticised Norway for not awarding him the Nobel Peace Prize, claiming he deserved the honour eight times for the wars
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Friday criticised Norway for not awarding him the Nobel Peace Prize, claiming he deserved the honour eight times for the wars he said he had settled.Addressing a rally in Syracuse, Trump also claimed to have saved 50 million lives by preventing India and Pakistan from going to war.“The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel peace prize, but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway, and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump said.“The Nobel peace prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilisation. We will not forget, Norway, that you didn’t give this prize,” the US President added.Trump then listed the conflicts he claimed to have resolved, adding that he was working to end two more, involving Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war.“We will not forget Norway, that you didn't give this prize with the greatest record in history — eight wars, we should have had 8 Nobel Prizes for each war— but that you didn't give the Nobel Prize for Peace to the United States of America,” he added.“Additionally, I stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon and blowing up the entire Middle East and ultimately far beyond the Middle East, including Europe, perhaps the US and I saved more lives than anyone in history,” Trump said.The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South African former UN human rights chief Navi Pillay, whom Trump dismissed as someone “nobody ever heard of”.“The Nobel Prize was given out today (Friday) to a liberal person who works at the United Nations, who nobody has ever heard of. I've never heard of the person, but congratulations anyway,” Trump said.Pillay, 85, is a South African-born jurist and former UN human rights chief who won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work promoting international law. She served as an International Criminal Court (ICC) judge from 2003 to 2008 and later chaired a UN commission that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, a finding strongly rejected by Israel.Four US presidents have received the Nobel Peace Prize: Theodore Roosevelt, Woodrow Wilson, Jimmy Carter and Barack Obama. Obama won the award in 2009, his first year in office.Trump has repeatedly criticised Obama’s win, arguing that he “got a prize for doing nothing”.Meanwhile, the Donald Trump administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, hours after former court judge Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote international law.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the sanctions were intended to prevent the ICC from prosecuting American citizens. The move marks a further escalation in the administration’s campaign against the Hague-based court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Indianapolis rebuilt a 10,000-foot airport runway using concrete that captures CO2 and stores it inside the pavement
articles.summary: Indianapolis International Airport rebuilt its 10,000-foot-long Runway 5R-23L with concrete designed to capture and permanently store carbon dioxide
articles.body: Indianapolis International Airport rebuilt its 10,000-foot-long Runway 5R-23L with concrete designed to capture and permanently store carbon dioxide inside the pavement. The $190 million reconstruction project introduced carbon-capture technology to an entire airport runway after receiving approval from the Federal Aviation Administration. The Indianapolis Airport Authority said the project was recognised with the Envision Platinum Award, the highest level awarded by the Institute for Sustainable Infrastructure. It combined the new concrete system with recycled construction materials, renewable energy and upgrades intended to improve the runway for decades.How the 10,000-foot runway captures and stores CO2The central innovation is the use of CarbonCure technology in the concrete. According to Engineering News-Record, the system introduces recycled carbon dioxide into freshly mixed concrete during production. The gas then undergoes mineralisation, turning it into a solid mineral and permanently embedding it in the pavement.The Sustainable Infrastructure report explains that the project uses post-industrial CO2 in fresh concrete, where it converts into calcium carbonate. The process is intended to reduce the amount of carbon associated with the concrete while also improving its compressive strength without affecting other important properties of the material.The 22-inch top concrete layer of the reconstructed runway contains the captured carbon. Engineering News-Record reported that the amount of carbon expected to be stored was equivalent to the carbon associated with planting about 1.2 million trees.This was not simply a small demonstration section. The FAA approved the use of the technology across the full 10,000-foot-long and 150-foot-wide runway, making the project a significant step for the use of carbon-capture concrete in airfield construction.The runway was rebuilt for long-term serviceRunway 5R-23L is an important part of Indianapolis International Airport because it handles most of the airport's cargo operations as well as a substantial amount of commercial airline traffic. The Sustainable Infrastructure report describes it as a 150-foot-wide, 10,000-foot-long runway forming part of the airport's southeast-side facilities.The reconstruction replaced the existing pavement with full-depth Portland cement concrete and included changes to the taxiway, drainage, markings, signs, lighting and navigation equipment. Kimley-Horn reported that the wider project reconstructed more than 450,000 square yards of concrete pavement while adding new LED lighting, signs, a firefighting water line and upgraded navigation aids.The pavement was also designed with longevity in mind. Engineering News-Record reported that the existing runway, which was about 30 years old, was expected to have a 40-year life after reconstruction rather than the previous 20-year expectation. An analysis led the project team to increase the pavement depth by an inch.What happened to the old runway materialsMuch of the material removed during construction did not simply become waste. The Indianapolis Airport Authority said the existing runway concrete would be crushed on site and recycled into the new project.Kimley-Horn later reported that the wider project diverted nearly 690,000 tons of waste from landfill, achieving a diversion rate of more than 99%. Crushed concrete was reused as aggregate base material and pipe bedding, reducing the need to transport replacement materials.Other materials were also put to use. Signs and lighting removed from the project were transferred for reuse at other airports in Indiana. The project also used recycled non-potable water for activities including dust control, compaction and irrigation, reducing the use of drinking-quality water by 50%, according to Kimley-Horn.These measures made material reuse a major part of the reconstruction rather than treating sustainability as something limited to the concrete mix.Renewable energy added another layer of sustainabilityThe runway project also incorporated renewable energy. The Indianapolis Airport Authority said the reconstruction included a 1,000-kilowatt direct-current solar photovoltaic system along with battery storage.The Sustainable Infrastructure report estimated that the solar installation would generate 1,552,341 kilowatt-hours of electricity each year, compared with an estimated 419,060 kilowatt-hours required by the project itself. The surplus electricity was intended to serve other airfield electrical systems beyond the immediate construction area.Kimley-Horn reported that the completed project also included a 10-acre photovoltaic solar array and two battery storage systems. These systems were designed to supply power to the Midfield Vault and one of the airport's aircraft rescue and firefighting facilities.LED lighting and signage were another part of the work. Kimley-Horn projected that the updated system could reduce operational energy consumption by 31% compared with the previous system.The project earned the highest sustainability recognitionThe combination of carbon capture, material reuse, renewable energy and other measures helped the project receive the Envision Platinum Award from the Institute for Sustainable Infrastructure.The Indianapolis Airport Authority said the $190 million project was the first airfield project in the world to receive the Platinum designation.According to the Indianapolis Airport Authority, the project was expected to create more than 2,700 jobs, while economic analysis found that every dollar spent on the reconstruction would generate another $0.80 in economic activity in Marion County.Kimley-Horn described the project as a multi-year effort shaped by extensive coordination because Runway 5R-23L sits beside the airport's major FedEx cargo operation. Construction had to be phased carefully to limit disruption while maintaining safe airport operations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bill Gates says white trails behind planes are making the planet hotter; suggests ways to get rid of them
articles.summary: The white trails left behind by planes in the sky may look harmless, but some of them contribute to global warming.
articles.body: The white trails left behind by planes in the sky may look harmless, but some of them contribute to global warming. Microsoft founder Bill Gates has highlighted how these trails, known as condensation trails or contrails, trap heat in the atmosphere. Bill Gates recently posted on the website – Gates Notes where he said that preventing certain contrails could eliminate up to 2% of global warming. Gates also explained that while aircraft emissions from burning jet fuel are a major climate concern, they are not the only way planes contribute to rising temperatures. He said some contrails can remain in the sky for hours, spread out and turn into thin clouds that trap heat.Gates said avoiding these trails could be a relatively low-cost way to reduce aviation's impact on the climate while cleaner aircraft technologies and fuels are still being developed.How can changing flight paths help prevent warming contrailsContrails form when water vapour from aircraft engines meets the right combination of cold temperatures and humidity. Water freezes around tiny particles released by the engines, creating ice crystals that form the white trails seen behind planes. Most contrails disappear quickly and have little effect on the climate. However, some persist for hours and spread into high-altitude clouds known as cirrus clouds.These clouds can reflect sunlight back into space, but they also absorb heat that would otherwise escape from Earth.Bill Gates said persistent contrails are responsible for about half of the temperature increase caused by aviation. One way to prevent them is to change flight paths slightly so planes avoid areas of the atmosphere where persistent contrails are likely to form. Bill Gates said airlines could make these adjustments when preparing flight plans, usually four to eight hours before departure.According to Bill Gates, changing the routes of about 5% of flights worldwide could help avoid most of the regions where warming contrails form. He also said the changes could increase fuel use by as little as 0.1% when averaged across all flights.Gates estimated that avoiding contrails could cost less than $10 per tonne of emissions avoided, and possibly around $1 to $2. He compared this with $130 or more per tonne for sustainable aviation fuel, which can reduce the lifecycle emissions associated with flying.Bill Gates helped start non profit organisation to tackle the trail problemBill Gates said the next challenge is making contrail avoidance a standard part of airline operations. He helped start the nonprofit Contrails.org, which is researching the problem and developing free, open-source software to help airlines plan routes.Last year, Contrails.org worked with American Airlines and Google Research on more than 100 flights that used contrail avoidance. Gates also highlighted Operation Blue Skies, a UK government-backed study in which some flights passing through Shanwick airspace, west of the UK, will have their routes adjusted to avoid creating contrails.Gates acknowledged that he also flies on private planes. He said he takes responsibility for reducing the climate impact of his flights by using routes that avoid warming contrails, using sustainable aviation fuel and offsetting his family's aviation emissions.You use AI every day. articles.summary: MP Rajgarh: 20-year-old allegedly beheads 17-year-old girlfriend in forest; dies in truck collision while fleeing, police recover body and saw.
articles.body: Bhopal: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly murdered and beheaded by her boyfriend, 20, in MP’s Rajgarh district on Sept 30, but within hours of the killing, the youth died in a road accident while fleeing the area, police said. The girl’s seven-day-old body was recovered from the forest in Biaora on Tuesday, with her head found about 50 feet from the torso.The youth, identified as Ankit Malviya, allegedly took the girl into the forest after she travelled from Karedi to Rajgarh to meet him. Following an argument, he allegedly killed her with a saw and later called his cousin to tell him about the incident. Malviya then left the forest on his motorcycle but died after colliding with a truck, police said.Rajgarh SP Amit Tolani said the investigation had established that the two were in a relationship and that the girl had been murdered, while the youth suspected of killing her died in the road accident soon afterwards. However, the exact reason behind the killing was yet to be established.“Yes, there was a noose at the spot. We are trying to ascertain the actual reason behind the incident. The two were in a relationship,” Tolani said.The minor lived with her maternal uncle in Karedi village and had been reported missing at Rajgarh Kotwali police station on Sept 30. Police began tracing her movements and examined CCTV footage from the area. The footage showed her travelling towards Shamsherpura on a motorcycle with Malviya, a resident of Jamonia Ganesh village.Malviya worked at a factory in Pithampur and had allegedly been in contact with the girl for around two years. Police said he had asked her to meet him on Sept 30. The girl travelled by bus from Karedi to Rajgarh, where she met Malviya. The two then travelled towards Biaora on his motorcycle.Police suspect the couple entered a forested area where an argument broke out. Malviya allegedly attacked the girl and severed her neck with a saw.After the alleged murder, police said, Malviya called his cousin and narrated what had happened. He then allegedly attempted suicide before leaving the forest.The investigation into Malviya’s call records showed that he had spoken to his cousin several times around the time of the incident. This eventually led police to question the cousin. While leaving the forest on his motorcycle, Malviya collided with a truck and died on the spot, police said.During questioning, the cousin allegedly told police about the information he had received from Malviya. articles.title: Psychology says children who immediately change the subject after being praised may have complicated feelings about attention
articles.summary: “You did such a good job!” a parent tells their child after seeing a drawing.
articles.body: “You did such a good job!” a parent tells their child after seeing a drawing. The child smiles briefly, then starts talking about a cartoon they watched or asks what is for dinner. Another child receives a compliment about a school performance but immediately begins discussing something that went wrong that day. Parents may find these reactions confusing. They have offered encouragement, so why does the child seem eager to move on? Do they feel embarrassed, dislike being the centre of attention or struggle to accept compliments?There is no single explanation. Some children feel shy when attention turns towards them. Others may be unsure how to respond, uncomfortable with being evaluated or simply more interested in the next thing on their mind. In some cases, the reaction may reflect how they have learned to understand praise and what they believe it says about them.Praise can feel like attention, not just appreciationFor adults, a compliment may seem like a straightforward way to make a child feel good. But children are also learning what praise means. Does it show that someone noticed their effort? Does it mean they are expected to do even better next time? Or does it put them in a position where they feel everyone is watching? A 2002 review examined research on how praise affects children's motivation. The authors concluded that praise can help or undermine motivation depending on how it is delivered and interpreted. Praise is more likely to be helpful when it feels sincere, supports a child's sense of competence and does not rely too heavily on comparisons with others.This does not mean that a child who changes the subject dislikes praise. It does suggest that a compliment may carry different meanings for different children. A child who feels awkward when praised may need time to get used to receiving positive attention, while another may simply prefer a quieter response.When praise creates pressure to keep performingConsider a child who wins a school competition. Everyone celebrates, relatives call to congratulate them, and parents repeatedly describe them as exceptionally talented. The next time the child takes part in a competition, the praise may feel less like recognition of what they have done and more like an expectation to repeat the success. Research has examined how the intensity of praise relates to children's self-perception. A 2017 study followed 120 parent-child pairs in the Netherlands, with children aged 7 to 11.The researchers found that inflated praise, expressions that exaggerated how good a child was, predicted lower self-esteem over time. It also predicted higher narcissism among children who already had high self-esteem. Ordinary, non-inflated praise did not predict either outcome. The findings do not show that children who change the subject are responding to pressure. However, they highlight why constant, exaggerated compliments are not necessarily more helpful than specific, proportionate encouragement. For a child who already worries about meeting expectations, being told “You're the smartest child in the class” may feel different from hearing “You worked hard to understand that problem.” The first comment makes a broad claim about the child; the second recognises something they did.Some children may find it difficult to accept a complimentChildren also learn how to respond to praise through social experience. Some may have heard adults encourage modesty, while others may worry that accepting a compliment will make them appear boastful. A child might therefore laugh, deny the compliment or redirect the conversation rather than say thank you. Research on children's understanding of modesty offers some context. In a 2000 study, researchers examined how children aged 6 to 10 responded to praise in hypothetical situations. Children aged eight and older showed a preference for modest responses and were more likely to justify them in terms of how others might judge a person. The researchers also found links between children's views of modesty and their sensitivity to social situations.How parents can respond without making praise uncomfortableIf a child regularly changes the subject after receiving a compliment, parents do not need to insist that they accept it or explain their reaction immediately. Instead, they can make praise more specific and less overwhelming. Rather than saying, “You're brilliant at everything,” try, “I noticed how carefully you worked on that drawing.” This acknowledges the child's effort without turning one achievement into a statement about their entire identity.Parents can also avoid repeatedly asking, “Why are you changing the subject? Can't you take a compliment?” Such questions may turn a small moment of discomfort into another situation in which the child feels watched. If the child moves on, it is usually fine to follow the new conversation. If the pattern seems persistent, a gentle question in a relaxed moment may help: “Do you feel awkward when people praise you, or would you rather they didn't make a big deal of it? The answer may be simple. The child may feel shy, dislike public attention or not know what to say. Parents should listen without assuming that the behaviour reveals low self-esteem or a deeper emotional difficulty.A change of subject on its own is not a warning sign. What matters more is the wider pattern: whether the child seems distressed by positive attention, repeatedly puts themselves down or becomes unusually anxious about making mistakes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Award-winning video of  child’s lungs sparks AI controversy: What gave it away, and how did it differ from the original?
articles.summary: Imagine looking through a microscope and discovering a world that seems almost impossible.
articles.body: Imagine looking through a microscope and discovering a world that seems almost impossible. Tiny hairs sway above a colourful landscape of red, purple and blue structures.But then a scientist notices something odd. Some structures seem to appear and disappear. Others move in ways that do not make biological sense. What looks like a remarkable window into the human body may be showing viewers something that the underlying experiment never actually established.That question turned a prize-winning microscopy video into an international scientific controversy. The video, which showed tiny hair-like structures called cilia in the airway of a child with a rare respiratory condition, was initially declared the winner of Nikon’s Small World in Motion competition. On October 9, 2026, Nikon disqualified the entry after concluding that it violated the contest’s rules on generative artificial intelligence.What was the award-winning video supposed to show?The video was submitted by Dr Ning Xu, an optical engineering researcher whose work was associated with Tsinghua University in China. It was presented as footage of beating airway cilia taken from a child with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a rare inherited condition that affects the way cilia are formed or function.Cilia are tiny, hair-like projections found on cells lining parts of the respiratory tract. They move in coordinated waves, pushing mucus towards the throat so the body can clear dust, bacteria and other particles trapped in it. When cilia do not work properly, mucus can build up in the airways. People with PCD may experience repeated lung, sinus and ear infections, and some develop lasting lung damage. The US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute estimates that the condition affects around one in 10,000 to 30,000 people.Watching cilia under a microscope can help specialists investigate the condition. Their shape, length and movement can offer important diagnostic clues.That is what made the video so compelling. It appeared to turn an invisible biological process into something viewers could see with their own eyes.What gave the video away?According to Nature, microscopy specialists began questioning the video soon after it was announced as the winner in September 2026. Their concerns centred on structures beneath the cilia that appeared biologically implausible.Edward Phelps, a bioengineering researcher at the University of Florida, raised questions about the purple structures. They appeared to resemble mitochondria, the components of cells that help produce energy. Yet their apparent size, arrangement and location did not make sense as the structures they seemed to represent.Other researchers questioned the blue and red features. Some structures appeared to change or disappear abruptly, while others seemed to move in ways that scientists would not expect from the biological material being shown.Dr Robert Hirst, a University of Leicester scientist who works on diagnosing PCD, also questioned the footage. Speaking to the BBC, he said the cells and cilia did not resemble those he had seen in patients with the condition.How was the AI version different from the original?Xu acknowledged using an unsupervised neural network for AI-assisted post-processing. He said the model was applied to reconstructed greyscale data to distinguish and colour structures with similar appearances. He maintained that AI had not generated the experimental movie, the cilia or their movement.In other words, he disputed the suggestion that the entire recording had been invented. His explanation was that AI had been used after the initial imaging to improve the visual presentation of features beneath the cilia.Why Nikon withdrew the awardNikon’s Small World in Motion competition celebrates videos made using light microscopes. Its rules explicitly prohibit AI-generated videos and allow the organisers to request original footage for verification.After the questions about Xu’s entry emerged, Nikon reviewed the video, supporting material and feedback from members of its judging panel.On October 9, the company said it had determined that the winning entry did not comply with its rules on generative AI. It disqualified the video and updated the rankings.The new first-place winner was Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam, whose video featured a tiny roundworm and a single-celled organism called Dileptus.Nikon said its decision concerned the entry’s eligibility under the competition rules. It stressed that the decision should not be interpreted as a judgement of Xu’s professional reputation, scientific contributions or intent. "After thoroughly re-evaluating the video and supporting materials and consulting with members of our judging panel, Nikon has determined that the winning video did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI. Nikon has adjusted the competition rankings to reflect this decision," it said.The company also acknowledged that advances in imaging and AI had created new challenges and said the incident highlighted the need to revisit its rules and evaluation procedures.The bigger question: Can we still trust what we see?The controversy has consequences beyond one competition. Scientific images help researchers communicate discoveries, teach students and explain illnesses to patients and families. Their power comes partly from the belief that they represent something observed in the real world.AI may become a valuable tool for scientific imaging. It can help analyse complex data and make difficult-to-see structures easier to examine.A microscope can reveal a world that the naked eye cannot see. AI can make that world easier to understand. But if the processing creates structures that viewers mistake for biological facts, the image risks becoming less informative precisely because it looks so convincing.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka detained from Delhi airport ahead of Jantar Mantar  protest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday at the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police on Saturday at the IGI Airport.Dipke had earlier said he was prepared to face arrest as he travelled to Delhi for the party’s proposed Jantar Mantar protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah of using security restrictions to prevent people from joining the demonstration.Questioning the deployment of security forces and restrictions on public movement, Dipke alleged that the government feared young people and citizens challenging its actions.At least 600 people have been detained under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act as security was tightened across the national capital ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, demanding Kumar’s resignation.Stringent traffic restrictions came into force at 6 am, with diversions planned at several locations across Delhi. Police personnel were deployed at barricades and key intersections to check vehicles and monitor movement around the protest site. The heightened security coincided with restrictions on metro services, train cancellations and the suspension of mobile internet services in parts of the capital.The Delhi Traffic Police warned of possible disruptions around Connaught Place, Mandi House, Jantar Mantar, Patel Chowk and other key intersections in central Delhi, with diversions to be regulated according to the prevailing law and order situation.According to the traffic advisory, affected stretches include the Ashoka Road-Jantar Mantar Road roundabout, Tolstoy Marg-Janpath crossing, Jai Singh Road-Sansad Marg crossing, Rail Bhawan roundabout, Patel Chowk, Gol Dak Khana and Windsor Place.Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed demonstration, citing law and order concerns and the possibility of inconvenience to residents. In its communication to the party, police said CJP’s intimation did not qualify as a duly filed application for permission.Under police guidelines, applications to hold demonstrations at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days in advance. Authorities also cited alleged past violations of protest conditions, including demonstrations continuing beyond the stipulated time limits.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Animals' ending explained: Ben Affleck and Kerry Washington-starrer makes OTT debut; Mark Kimball’s motivation behind sinister plot?
articles.summary: Ben Affleck is back with yet another thrilling adventure with the OTT film, 'Animals.' While the plot of the movies centers around a kidnapping, as it
articles.body: Ben Affleck is back with yet another thrilling adventure with the OTT film, 'Animals.' While the plot of the movies centers around a kidnapping, as it slowly unravels, viewers find out that the controversy runs deeper.Ben Affleck’s ‘Animals’ ending explainedThe premise of the film revolves around a wealthy Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose life implodes when a kidnapping case exposes a dark web of deception. Affleck, who stars in the film, has also directed and co-written the script. He plays the role of Mark Kimball, an independent candidate for mayor of Los Angeles. On the front he is picture perfect; however, behind the polished image, he is struggling financially. His marriage to psychologist Abigail is nearing its end, and both of them are keeping secrets from one another.Things start to unravel after Mark receives a call telling him that his son Denny, who is played by Christopher Woodley, has been kidnapped. The kidnapper demands USD 7 million for his release, warning Mark not to pull any moves since he is under surveillance. Mark’s son had been out on Halloween, trick-o-treating with the housekeeper’s son, Hector.However, he no longer has that kind of money since his mayoral campaign has been struggling. Not only that but Mark has also used up almost all of his family savings for the campaign without telling Abigail about it. Later, his campaign manager Sam helps him connect with Dayle Burton, played by Gillian Anderson, a fixer who is capable of paying the ransom amount. However, she tells Mark that she wants another USD 1.4 million on top of the USD 7 million, to which Mark agrees and puts their house up as collateral.SPOILERS AHEADDenny was never kidnappedHowever, just as the Kimballs are about to contact the kidnapper about the money being arranged, Denny walks back into the house. It turns out that he and Hector had been wearing the same exact outfits for Halloween, and he had simply separated from the two in the crowd. This confirms that rather than Hector, the kidnappers have instead taken Hector by mistake.Hector's father, Ramon, arrives at Mark and Abigail’s home with an injured Cecilia, and Mark receives a video of Hector, who is being held captive. The Kimballs first contemplate whether they should pay the ransom for Hector; however, Mark realizes that he needs the support of the Latino community for his campaign and how Ramon is undocumented. His campaign manager also tells him that he will be ridiculed publicly if he refuses to save Hector. Reluctantly, they agree to pay the USD 7 million to the kidnappers to save his housekeeper’s son.Dayle later advises Mark that he can either wait for the police, pay the amount and hope Hector is released, or kill the kidnappers. Ramon also takes things on himself after Mark confesses that they are being watched. He roams around the neighborhood and manages to find one of the kidnappers; however, during their altercation, they manage to escape.Do they manage to save Hector?Mark and Dayle drive to the ransom exchange at the concrete-lined Los Angeles River, deciding that instead of waiting for the police and legalities, the kidnappers need to be killed to end the ordeal and save his political career. They see two men along with Hector. One of the men wearing a rabbit mask throws Hector down into the channel, where Mark catches him. When they try to kill the two, Dayle’s armed assassin, Rand, is on standby and shoots the two kidnappers. However, a third kidnapper appears and shoots both Rand and Dayle. Just when he is about to attack Mark and Hector, Ramon rushes in and shoots the third and final kidnapper.What does the ‘Animals’ ending mean?In the ending, though it is Ramon who kills the final kidnapper and saves Hector and Mark, the politician still controls the narrative. He buys the family’s silence by paying them the ransom amount while he comes out of the situation victorious and with an inspirational story at hand to help run his mayoral campaign. Mark also destroys evidence that Dayle had on him for ordering the hit on the kidnappers.You can watch and stream the 2026 crime thriller ‘Animals’ on Netflix.

articles.title: Virgo Weekly Shani Horoscope: Partnerships Need Patience This Week
articles.summary: Virgo's closest bonds come under quiet review this week, and the best results come from talking things through.
articles.body: Virgo's closest bonds come under quiet review this week, and the best results come from talking things through. Shani, moving backward in Pisces, your seventh, tests both marriage and business partnerships. Navratri softens the mood, though, and an old misunderstanding may finally clear.Retrograde Shani in the House of PartnersRetrograde planets return to unfinished matters. In the seventh, that often means a promise made to a spouse or a clause in a business agreement.A partner may ask why something was delayed or changed. Answer honestly and without defensiveness. Shani in this house respects reliability, so small acts of follow-through matter more than speeches.Talk Before You DecideMercury, your ruler, sits in Libra, your second house of speech, with retrograde Venus. Use that combination to speak gently but clearly.Before committing to a new business contract or a joint loan, discuss it fully. From 24 October, your ruler moves backwards, and misunderstandings rise, so settle key decisions in the coming days.An Old Misunderstanding ClearsMidweek, with the Moon in your third house of communication, a frank talk comes more easily. A disagreement from months ago, perhaps about money or relatives, can be resolved if you listen first. Exalted Jupiter in your eleventh brings goodwill from friends who know both sides.On Saturday the Sun finally leaves Virgo. Shani's full aspect has weighed on it all month, and its departure lifts some tension from your mood, though it turns debilitated in your second.Kalaratri and Shared WorshipSaturday's Kalaratri puja is a good time for couples to pray together. Kalaratri removes fear, including the fear of losing a relationship. Offer the goddess rice sweetened with jaggery.Do's for the WeekAnswer your partner's questions honestly.Settle key decisions before 24 October.Don'ts for the WeekAvoid signing joint loans in a hurry.Do not interrupt during a frank talk.Shani Remedy for the WeekLight two lamps side by side at a Shani shrine on Saturday, one for you and one for your partner. articles.body: NEW DELHI: “Even Indira Gandhi didn't do this,” Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke said in a video shared by the party after he and fellow leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday ahead of the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar.In the video, Dipke is also heard saying, “Arrest hone liye hi aaya hu.”In a statement, the party condemned the alleged detentions, claiming they were part of a pre-planned move to prevent its leaders from reaching the site of their proposed protest.CJP described the action as a violation of freedom of movement and demanded the immediate and unconditional release of the three leaders.The CJP has called the proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and changes relating to Form 6, used for voter registration.The detentions came amid heightened security across the national capital, with police deploying personnel at key locations and authorities imposing restrictions on transport services ahead of the demonstration.(This is a developing story)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
